analysis.overview: Introductory undergraduate textile design course (6 UOC, Term 2, Paddington campus) introducing the narrative and storytelling aspects of textiles via patterns, materials and construction. Students integrate hand and digital design methods, consider social, cultural, environmental and sustainable themes, apply industry-appropriate research methodologies, and are encouraged to experiment, learn from failure and take creative risks to develop cohesive conceptually-based textiles.

topics.title: Textile Fibres, Structures and Processes
learning_outcomes: Identify and describe textile fibres, structures and processes using language and terminology of the textiles industry
topics.source_evidence: CLO1: Identify and describe textile fibres, structures and processes

topics.title: Constructed Textile Techniques
learning_outcomes: Learn techniques to construct experimental textiles
Document processes and reflect on opportunities and challenges
topics.source_evidence: Weeks 1-4 Studio: Plying Fibres, Weave & Interlacing, Hand Knitting, Felting

topics.title: Stitch and Fabric Manipulation
learning_outcomes: Apply stitching and fabric manipulation techniques in experimental textile making
topics.source_evidence: Week 5: Hand Stitch, Sewing Machine Stitch & Fabric Manipulation

topics.title: Surface Patterning and Colouring Cloth
subtopics: Screen printing with ink and mordants
learning_outcomes: Learn techniques to colour and pattern cloth
Document and reflect on each technique in a journal
topics.source_evidence: Weeks 7-9: Handstitch, Applique & Patchwork; Screen Printing with Ink and Mordants

topics.title: Natural Dye and Thermoplastics
learning_outcomes: Apply natural dye and thermoplastic techniques in textile experimentation
topics.source_evidence: Week 10: Natural Dye & Thermoplastics Induction: Dye Lab

topics.title: Sustainable and Circular Textile Practices
learning_outcomes: Implement circular practices to transform textile waste through experimental textile techniques
Develop a sustainable narrative as a value-led designer
topics.source_evidence: REMAKE CHALLENGE to transform textile waste, saving it from landfill

topics.title: Practice-Based Research and Documentation
subtopics: Research into textile artists' and designers' practices
Investigation of textile theorists and writers
learning_outcomes: Conduct practice-based research into textile artists'/designers' practices
Reflect on experimental textiles using documentation and evaluation methods appropriate to the textiles design industry
topics.source_evidence: CLO2: Conduct practice-based research into textile artist's/designer's practices

topics.title: Conceptual and Narrative Textile Design
subtopics: Storytelling via patterns, materials and construction
Cohesive conceptual basis and design narrative
Local textile practitioner culture inspiring surface designs
learning_outcomes: Design and create textiles with an integrated/cohesive conceptual basis/design narrative
topics.source_evidence: CLO3: Design and create textiles with an integrated/ cohesive conceptual basis

study_notes: Minimum 80% attendance is required for all tutorials, seminars, studios and workshops; failure to meet this results in a Fail (FL) regardless of performance in assessment tasks
Assessment 1 is introduced in Week 1; Assessment 2 is introduced in Week 5

Both assessments use AI mode 'Assistance with Attribution': the first iteration must be the student's own work, and any generative AI output used must be fully referenced or risk academic misconduct referral
Neither assessment is a Turnitin assignment
Late submission penalty: 5% per calendar day, capped at five days, after which no submission is accepted
A Textiles 1 Material Kit (~$29, price may vary) is available to purchase in the first weeks of term via EFTPOS
Students should organise listed materials and equipment (A4 binder, unlined journal 210gsm+, drawing/painting supplies, sewing equipment) before Week 1
This course is a prerequisite for DDES2160 Textile Design 2 and DDES2161 Textile Design 3
Week 6 is a non-teaching week; there are no classes in Weeks 11 and 12 (Assessment 2 submission in Week 12)
Feedback is provided regularly in studio through discussion with peers and tutors; summative feedback is digital and rubric-based
